summary: Retest of iteration_380: both HIGH issues are FIXED. Full-tree sweep confirms exactly ONE remaining binary-write hit: routes_references.py:151 temp_path.write_bytes(contents) inside tempfile.TemporaryDirectory (PROCESSING_TEMP_FILE, correct). No other module writes uploaded content to container-local disk — all remaining `open(...,'w')` matches are text-mode JSON app-state or audit logs. object_storage.build_object_key delegates to build_named_object_key; safe_basename strips traversal. SURFACE_POLICIES includes 'operation-payment-receipts' with image+PDF only. INVALID classifications verified correct (a .MOV video, .txt files, and text-bytes files falsely named .pdf on image/pdf-only surfaces). `--apply` alone REFUSED with 'REFUSED: --apply also requires --i-understand-this-writes'. No os.remove/os.unlink/shutil.rmtree/shutil.move in the migration script. Destructive guard fail-closed re-confirmed live on preview: DELETE /api/operations => 403 destructive_operations_disabled, POST /api/admin/reset-inventory => 403 same, both with correlation_id. Hostile filenames against /api/operations/{op_id}/payment-receipts/{filename} (../../../etc/passwd and ..%2F..%2Fsecret.png) both return 404 — safe. Legacy on-disk file counts sanity-check EXACT match to owner's readings: vehicles 10/13780969, finance_audit_evidence 9/37014, operation_payment_receipts 6/24860, custom_templates 3/8197309. Backend health 200, no import/circular errors in supervisor logs after adding `from core import object_storage` to routes_extended.py and routes_templates.py. Login + /api/auth/me + vehicles list + operations list all 200; no raw MongoDB `_id` in vehicles response. critical_code_review_comments: Both HIGH findings from iteration_380 are correctly fixed. routes_templates.py:upload_template is now object-storage backed with content verification; routes_extended.py:_save_operation_payment_receipt is now async, awaited, content-verified, and uses a deterministic named object key so the public URL contract /api/operations/{op_id}/payment-receipts/{filename} is preserved unchanged.

object_storage.build_named_object_key correctly funnels the caller-provided name through safe_basename() which strips path separators and control chars — a hostile receipt filename cannot cross the entity_id/surface boundary in the object key.

Serving route get_operation_payment_receipt applies _safe_filename() before building the object key AND before touching the legacy local path (join uses the sanitised name), so ../../../etc/passwd and ..%2F..%2Fsecret.png both resolve to a nonsense sibling key and return 404 with no bytes served.

SURFACE_POLICIES['operation-payment-receipts'] deliberately excludes video (matches the migration script's INVALID classification of the .MOV in the sweep) and text (matches INVALID for .txt receipts), so the storage layer never widens the pre-existing 'image or PDF only' product rule for payment evidence.

Migration script remains fail-safe: --dry-run is default, --apply is REFUSED without --i-understand-this-writes, no destructive filesystem ops anywhere, CONFLICT is surfaced instead of silent overwrite.

Only one PROCESSING_TEMP_FILE remains in the codebase (routes_references.py:151), and it lives inside a tempfile.TemporaryDirectory context manager that guarantees cleanup on both success and exception paths. Not a persistence surface.

rca of the issue: Not a bug this iteration — this is the successful closure of the two HIGH persistent-upload-surface misses reported in iteration_380. Root fix: the developer added `from core import object_storage` to both files, rewrote upload_template to use validate_upload+put_object with content verification and dropped the shutil.copyfileobj + local file_path write, and rewrote _save_operation_payment_receipt to be async with build_named_object_key so the deterministic URL contract survives the migration. Both fixes preserve the existing HTTP surface (same routes, same URL shapes, same accepted extensions) — no product-level widening was introduced.
